verses.text: A psalm by Asaph. The Mighty One, God, the LORD, speaks and summons the whole earth from sunrise to sunset.
God shines out from Zion, perfect in beauty.
Our God comes and won’t stay silent. Fire devours everything ahead of him, and a fierce storm rages around him.
He calls to the heavens above and to the earth as he comes to judge his people:
“Gather my faithful ones to me, those who made a covenant with me by sacrifice.”
The heavens declare his righteousness, because God himself is the judge. Selah.
“Listen, my people, and I’ll speak. Israel, I’ll testify against you. I am God, your God.
I have no complaint about your sacrifices. Your burnt offerings are always before me.
I don’t need a bull from your stall or male goats from your pens.
Every animal in the forest is mine, along with the cattle on a thousand hills.
I know every bird in the mountains, and all the wild animals of the fields are mine.
If I were hungry, I wouldn’t tell you. The world and everything in it belong to me.
Do I eat the flesh of bulls or drink the blood of goats?
Offer thanks to God as your sacrifice and keep the vows you made to the Most High.
Call on me when trouble comes. I’ll rescue you, and you’ll honor me.”
But God says to the wicked, “What right have you to recite my laws or speak my covenant,
when you hate correction and toss my words aside?
You see a thief and join in. You make common cause with adulterers.
You give your mouth over to evil, and your tongue spins lies.
You sit and speak against your brother. You slander your own mother’s son.
You did all this while I kept quiet, and you thought I was just like you. Now I’ll rebuke you and lay the charges out before your eyes.
Think about this, you who forget God, or I’ll tear you apart and no one will rescue you.
Those who offer thanks as a sacrifice honor me. To those who set their path right I’ll show the salvation of God.”
